title: In Stars And Time
body:
In Stars And Time reminded me why I fell in love with Indie turn-based RPGs. It’s the feelings, the goals, the characters. This game made me feel that I was part of that world and its story. I wanted to see it end. And in the end I didn’t want it to end. This game made me laugh, wonder, fear and cry many many times. A bit like how every good dish contains a little bit of all the different basic flavors. That’s In Stars And Time for you.

What makes this game stand out are the characters and the concept of time and loops and how it’s explained in this context. Every character in your party is so deep and well written with very interesting backgrounds but also keeping them simple to understand and relate to. Especially relate to. Also the main character aka you or Siffrin is so well written with the mysteriousness. Not knowing about him/them relates well to the fact that you are joining this world completely blind as well.

The concept of time and loops first might seem a bit boring at first but man, In Stars And Time executes it perfectly. Looping in time is not boring at all. And the way it’s explained to you in a very simple way makes the game super enjoyable from the start to the end. I’m not here to explain it to you. Hard to explain anything without spoiling I guess.

And everything else. Just “super duper” good stuff. A perfect package I would say. Thanks to a random Reddit comment who suggested this game. This review doesn’t even scratch the surface of how good this game is. Play this hidden gem!

title: CONTROL Resonant
body:
Tuntuu vain oikealle kirjoittaa tämä arvio kunnon suomenkielellä. En koe itseäni kummemmin isänmaalliseksi, mutta kun Remedy julkaisee jotain uutta olen aina ostamassa sen heti. Kaikkien suomalaisten olisi oltava ylpeitä, että meillä on näin laadukas viihdetuote maailmanmarkkinoilla jälleen kerran. Toivon vain kovasti, että tämä myisi suuria määriä, että Remedy olisi kansamme seuraavatkin 31 vuotta.

Pelissä ei mielestäni ole mitään, mikä häiritsi minua. En itse ole mikään suurin Hack & Slash -peligenren fani, mutta Control Resonant piti minut todella koukussa 26 tunnin ajan. Ehkä siihen vaikutti se, että peli (etenkin alussa) oli todella haastava ja taistelutekniikat eivät olleet todella monimutkaisia. Pelin haastavuus onkin ehkä jopa yksi suosikki asioistani pelissä. Hieman pelistä tuli Elden Ring mieleen siinä mielessä, että on suositeltavaa tutkia muita alueita kartasta, jos viholliset ovat liian haastavia. (Ei mitenkään liity siihen, että Soulslike tyylinen peli koska sitä Control Resonant ei todellakaan ole). Skill treet ja päivitykset näyttivät aluksi todella laajoille ja monimutkaisille, mutta pelin edetessä ne olivat loistavasti tehty ja jättivät hyvin varaa tuleville läpipeluille eri buildien kehittämiseen. Gameplay kokonaisuudessa on siis todella omalaatuinen yhdistelmä, joka toimii loistavasti sen eri ympäristöissä.

Parhaiten pelistä jäi itselleni mieleen hieno Remedyn luoma maailma ja maisemat. Niin monta “Vau!” hetkeä. Vaikea nähdä minkään pelin tekevän samoin kun Remedy tekee maailman rakennuksen (world building?) suhteet. Omaperäistä laatua, kuten myös koko pelihän sitä on hehe. Tähän maailman rakennukseen yhdistettynä aivan täydellinen soundtrack ja tarinankerronta luovat jälleen kerran maailman, jota muista peleistä ei voi hakea. Soundtrack on aina Remedyllä aivan loistavaa laatua. Petri Alangon hieno sävellys yhdistettynä todella mielenkiintoiseen kattaukseen suomalaista musiikkia oli yhtä lailla yllättävä kokemus, kuten esimerkiksi Alan Wake 2:ssa. Tarinankerronta oli yhtä lailla todella mielenkiintoinen ja antoi paljon vastauksia ensimmäisen Control-pelin kysymyksiin. Koskettava ja omituinen tarinan jatko sai vain ajattelemaan, että “Hitsi, tässä me sitä nyt ollaan jatkamassa tätä tarinaa seitsemän vuotta myöhemmin.”

Kyseessä siis on täydellinen paketti, 10/10 mestariteos (Vähän kuin tämä olisi Remedylle jotain uutta hehe). Kiitos koko Remedy tiimi. Rakastan teidän elämyksiänne ja tulen rakastamaan niitä varmasti jatkossa.

title: HITMAN World of Assassination
body:
Hitman World of Assassination is a massive package that offers dozens of hours of content. Very much bang for your buck if you know what to buy and when. I bought the standard edition for 30€ and a week after that the deluxe pack DLC for about 20€ on top of that. The Deluxe pack has some peak content for sure but some of it is so bad and boring. The Hitman 2 Expansion from the pack is the most important one and the best one, adding 2 extra maps. But what makes that stupid is that those 2 maps are mandatory if you want to beat the full story of the Hitman games fully since those are canon and set before the 3rd game. Very weird and stupid if you are really into playing this for the story. The story is great for sure especially in the 3rd game but I know you ain't buying this for that reason.

Gameplay is simply amazing. Stealthing is executed so well. The best part about it is easily the free will to approach missions in your own way. So many ways to assassinate targets gives this game so much replay value. And rewarding that replay with satisfying progression and new items is the cherry on top. Taking all that freedom away makes the game very boring (I’m looking at you 7 Deadly Sins DLC). And also, if you get bored with that there is still the freelancer gamemode which technically adds an endless amount of replayability. What an amazing package for its price. (When you buy it on sale ofc)

So yeah the game at its core is great but outside of that, there are some flaws. No game really makes you watch a YouTube tutorial on which version to buy. This one made me do that lol. And if you put older games to the newer one as a complete package why can’t you add the DLC from the older games into that package as well?! Some of the weirdest marketing tactics I have ever seen. Also this game crashes a lot on my end. Overall a great game. One of the best of its genre. 9/10.

title: METAL GEAR SOLID 4: Guns of the Patriots - Master Collection Version
body:
There is no better game to conclude a saga than Metal Gear Solid 4. Playing every MGS game beforehand makes this one of the most rewarding video game experiences there is. Everything pays off in this game, every damn MGS title. This game made me laugh, smile, tear up and everything in between. What an experience.

I don’t really see any major flaws in this game. The gameplay is the good old we know from Metal Gear Solid 3 but elevated into even greater heights with very interesting new concepts like the OctoCamo and the Metal Gear Mk. II. The visuals of the PS3 are very well enhanced with this Master Collection release and the game runs butter smooth. Well done Konami.

My guess is that many people don’t like the lack of actual gameplay in this title since the game is apparently about 40% cutscenes. But I don’t really see it as an issue. It’s a design choice. And man I enjoy a story told well. You ain’t just buying a Hideo Kojima game to play the game. You are there to experience cinema. You are there to experience something no video game developer does. Thank you Kojima-san for this journey I decided to start this year.

So yeah, it’s a masterpiece, 10/10, maybe in my top 25 games of all time or something. Just play Metal Gear Solid. *mic drop*

title: Crypt of the NecroDancer
body:
Once you start to get good at this game it becomes one of the best roguelikes you've played. Crypt of the Necrodancer is such a simple looking game but from the inside it's one of the most satisfying and complex game's there is.

The gameplay's premise is quite simple. Defeat enemies to the beat of the music and advance the simple looking dungeons downwards facing bosses on the way. But once you start playing the difficulty hits very very hard. And it's also quite fast. Taking your time one zone at a time to master every enemy movement and attack gives me the same kind of satisfaction souls-like games give me when I learn boss and enemy patterns. Game just takes time and rewards you well once you get good.

The game's soundtrack is also one of the best things about it. A rhythm game cannot be a good game if the soundtrack doesn't match the same quality. With Crypt of the Necrodancer there is no song that misses. What a banger!

Cannot wait to play more of this. One successful run just isn't enough. There is so much to this game. And I haven't even bought a single DLC. Truly an indie classic.

title: Slay the Princess — The Pristine Cut
body:
I usually write somewhat long reviews for games but with Slay the Princess it's impossible. It's really hard to describe... ...anything.

A psychological experiment. Easily one of my favorite games of all time.

Man I love to play video games for the experiment. And you should as well. Try different genres, different experiences. It will open your mind and heart.
verdict: I even have a physical artbook of this game

title: Hi-Fi RUSH
body:
Hi-Fi Rush is a game where you're an annoying kid trying to take down Sam Altman by playing Devil May Cry to the beat of the music. The game is a solid package all around and it screams that it's an passion project from the developers.

Easily my favorite part about this game are the animations. Everything is so well baked and mastered to perfection. And also implementing those animations so smoothly to the gameplay was just cinema.

Gameplay is basically just the usual "GOOD (VERY GOOD)" hack and slash combat except you deal more damage when you do your hits to the beat. It's simply fun and satisfying. Sometimes it felt a bit repetitive but still fun. So yeah just a simple idea turned into a banger game. That's all there is to it.

Story and characters are easily the weakest part in my opinion. The story is very predictable. Play this one for the gameplay. Characters are hit or misses, mostly misses. The main character Chai is intentionally annoying I get that but it doesn't really change my opinion about the character. Also the dialogue is most of the time pretty basic and corny. Maybe that's also the point? I don't really know. Just wasn't for me I guess...

But overall the game is great. Another one of those games that really shows the developers' passion and dedication. If you enjoy hack and slash and rhythm games you will feel right at home with this one. Solid 9/10.

title: Dispatch
body:
There isn't really anything bad about this game. Playing this game just makes you feel like you are watching a great superhero animated series where you control how the story evolves. Such a smooth experience all the way through. And the dispatching gameplay added on top of that doesn't have a negative impact on the experience at all. Gameplay is very engaging and fun. The tiniest nitpick I have is that I reached the max level way too fast. Maybe just a me problem.

I paid around 20 euros for this game and it only being a bit under 10 hours long might sound like it's not worth the money but take it like this. How much money would you pay for a good movie or a tv show? That's right. 15-20 bucks. And do not forget this game is an indie project with super passionate developers and super talented cast of voice actors. And it has a lot of replay value. Dispatch is one of the best experiences for its price, easily. 10/10

title: UNBEATABLE
body:
Sometimes this game feels a bit rough around the edges, but at other times, it is pure CINEMA. UNBEATABLE is one of the most passionately made games I have ever played. Even though the game has its lows it still shows that these developers truly loved making this game. And that there might be what makes this game what it is.

UNBEATABLE being a rhythm game is clear. The gameplay is great. Nothing that crazy but very enjoyable. I can see true rhythm game fans enjoying this quite a bit. The game's story is also great even though it was a bit confusing at times especially near the end. But even with the confusion, the story was touching and I enjoyed it.

The game feeling a bit rough around the edges is the best way to describe its problems. The gameplay between actual rhythm segments felt a bit weird and sometimes confusing. Also having random dialogue not being voice acted in the middle of the conversation was a bit annoying. I get that not all of the dialogue must be voice acted especially for an indie game but having it happen in just the most random places was weird. Just a bunch of little things that made the experience a bit annoying.

But putting those problems aside, oh man the animations, music, and atmosphere were easily the best part about UNBEATABLE. Such an outstanding art style with masterful animations made watching this game cinema. I just wish there was more of this. Those hype moments where it starts with a cutscene and a banger rhythm game segment easily counter the negatives of this game. Truly a one of a kind game made with pure love. 9/10.

(Edit: After reconsideration it's a 10.)
verdict: I can't stand it, it's brain poison

title: What Remains of Edith Finch
body:
What Remains of Edith Finch is a really special game indeed. I bought this since I heard it's a unique experience and yeah sure it was. The story is well written and all but clearly the best thing about this game was it's execution as a video game. Every tale told in their own respectful and different way was very interesting to follow and made the gameplay more than just "walking simulator".

The story didn't really resonate with me that much even though it was a special one. But how story is told makes it truly stand out. Another one of those cases where the story is best told in a video game format.

I really hope these developers are cooking something even bigger and ambitious since this game really showcases what they are capable of. Play this more as an experience than as a game. Solid 8/10 for me.

title: DOOM: The Dark Ages | Revelations
body:
It's so sad that over half of id Software got laid off since this DLC is one of the best or maybe even the best DOOM experience there is. I thought it would be hard to top the base game's DOOM gameplay since it's my personal favorite out of the three new DOOM games but yeah, they made Dark Ages even better. Combining the heavy Dark Ages gameplay with Eternal style was combat was just a perfect idea. The Chain Spear is sooo satisfying to use. And upgrading it and adapting it to my kit felt so incredible. The stab was probably my favorite upgrade because having two melee weapons to hit demons to the face is just cinema. Also shoutout to the sound designers since those hit sounds were something else man.

Nothing really to say about the level design or levels in general. They weren't really anything special compared to the base game. Adding the spear and it's mechanics to puzzles was a nice feature I guess.

Soundtrack was of course A BANGER but didn't feel any different from the base game. Maybe I will change my mind after a couple of extra listens. No plans to buy the vinyl if they ever release one. (Edit: Yeah it's quite different actually)

My only nitpick is the post game content and achievements. With the base game I was able to earn my achievement badge in one playthrough which was super good stuff but now with this DLC there is this new End Game content. Classic Doom gameplay is fun and all but I don't really vibe with those time trials. It's cool that there is more to do after the DLC but I just wish I could have gotten my achievement badge back fairly easily.

But overall an easy recommendation for any modern DOOM fan. To put it simply it feels like Eternal + Dark Ages but it still stands on it's own. 20 bucks for this level of additional content is certainly a surprise. I was expecting it to be a bit more expensive.

title: 1000xRESIST
body:
After playing this game, it is hard to find words to describe it. This could be a great book. But also at the same time it would never. The gameplay is 50% walking and moving to places and 50% dialogue. But you will never play this game because it’s a video game. Playing 1000xRESIST means you are willing to observe and enjoy one of the best written sci-fi stories out there. No game has been like this for me. What a weird and interesting experience.

I played this game almost everyday, only 1 Chapter per day. It was a fun experimental idea which probably enhanced my experience. Having 24 hours to internalize what I had experienced made me understand the complex story more but also made me respect and value these types of “walking simulator” games in a different light. (Man I hate the term walking simulator) But of course near the end I couldn’t hold back. I needed to keep on playing.

It’s just so weird to give this game a rating. My 9/10 doesn’t really tell that this game is so peak. But I can’t give it a 10 since I’m ranking video games and well the gameplay is just what it is. Many times during my playthrough I thought that this would be an awesome game to adapt to a different medium but after beating it I don’t really see any way to make this any better. Video games just being video games are sometimes just the thing that makes those stories so impactful. (Like Ben Starr once said lol)

So yeah 1000xRESIST is one of a kind video game. 20 bucks for a thrilling sci-fi adventure like this is a steal.

title: Toree Saturn
body:
Toree Saturn just screams Sonic Adventure. Fast 3D platforming combined with Sega Saturn/Dreamcast style art and having literal Sonic music makes this game just pure fun. Game is sadly just about 30 minutes long if you don't bother collecting every collectible or reaching the best ranks in every level but maybe the length is part of the fun. And the game is just 2 bucks on sale. Basically a free game at that point. Worth the price EASILY.

There isn't really anything to complain about. The whole package is just so well put together. Solid 9/10 game.
verdict: How tf did they get Johnny Gioeli to sing in this?

title: Sekiro™: Shadows Die Twice - GOTY Edition
body:
If Bloodborne is about playing aggressively Sekiro adds patience to that. Executor Nightreign The Game is more than just a cool parrying game. It is its own work of art. It really makes me laugh that nowadays there are so many games coming out that look like Sekiro to me. This is the real “OG” souls samurai game and it’s SO PEAK.

At the start of my journey the game really felt like the Executor from Elden Ring Nightreign and yeah sure it is literally the same deflection mechanic but the deeper you go the game becomes more than that. One of the first things you’re going to notice is the unique level design. The much more vertical level design truly stands out and is in my opinion one of the highlights that makes Sekiro the game it is. Plus adding smooth grappling hook mechanics to that is just a cherry on top. (Not to mention the stealth combined with the level design.)

But without a doubt the most notable thing about this game is the combat. And oh man it’s SOOO PEAAKKK! Every single enemy is sooo well designed. Movesets are tough and very difficult to fight against but they are not badly designed. EVERY SINGLE TIME you are the problem. And that makes the game one of the best games ever made. YOU need to die over and over again to learn. The learning process in this game is more about learning than playing. Every soulborne is somewhat like that but Sekiro turns it up to eleven.

Also the way you level up your character is super unique and cool. First it felt weird of course but over time this also became very interesting and enjoyable. Killing minibosses for extra skills and items is such an awesome feature that makes challenging optional bosses somewhat mandatory. Combat arts were cool, sure but I didn’t find any crazy uses for them. But the prosthetic tools on the other hand were sick and made some really interesting gameplay scenarios.

I could go on and on with this review since there are so many little and awesome things to talk about. Sekiro Shadows Die Twice is just one of the best games ever made thanks to its perfect execution and unique combat design. It’s one of the most challenging games for a reason. You just have to learn the enemy and be patient and aggressive at the same time.

(Also if you’re getting into FromSoftware’s soulsborne games don’t start with this please. Some don’t even call this a soulslike. Sekiro is a way different case and way more challenging.)

title: Rift of the NecroDancer
body:
Never really played rhythm games but this really caught my eye. The unique gameplay, cool visuals and a banger soundtrack got me hooked to play this even more after I beat the (very simple and nothing special) story mode.

The gameplay is very addictive. Mastering songs to fully combo them or even beat them on higher difficulties feels amazing. Also every enemy type feels natural and great to play to. Configuring controls to your liking is very well done and easy to setup. Boss battles in the story are hit or miss mostly. The more difficult ones at the end were easily more enjoyable than the starting bosses. The minigames were okay and sometimes even bad. Just some fillers between sequences. But the story and minigames are not the true reason why you play this game, the rhythm gameplay is.

Visuals and the soundtrack are amazing. Love the simple and cartoony art style with all of the visuals and such. Soundtrack is very versatile consisting of mostly electronic and metal music. Can't really name favorites. Also the game has a lot of banger DLCs which expand the song catalogue even more. But what really expands it is the Steam Workshop support. You can basically play any of your favorite songs if there's a level for it. And if there isn't just make one. The level editor seems to be very beginner friendly.

So basically if you want to play rhythm games since you have never really played one, start with Rift of The NecroDancer. It's super enjoyable for a first timer. A lot of variety and great gameplay.

title: Cairn
body:
Cairn is a masterpiece with one of the most well baked climbing gameplay I've ever seen. They probably hired some top tier physicists to make the gameplay work. It's in some areas very difficult and stressful but you will make it through somehow. The dopamine rush you get when you finish a long climb just feels so good. Combine this with an emotional story, unique art style and stunning soundtrack, you got Cairn.

Furi already being one of my favorite games of all time, this was a no-brainer for me to play. The Game Bakers are such a talented team. Cannot wait what you guys will bake next.

Another 10/10 masterpiece.
verdict: Release the Make This Right remix pls

title: Spiritfarer®: Farewell Edition
body:
I cannot thank myself enough for pulling this out of my backlog and playing this. Easily in my top 10 best games ever made, maybe even in top 5. Simple but fun and always surprising gameplay loop with stunning animations, incredible soundtrack and heartwarming characters. And yeah the story or more like the game's message... It's just so perfectly executed and left me crying. Never have I felt this way about a video game. Thank you Thunder Lotus.

One of the few "this isn't your type of game but just play it" games.
verdict: My Game of The Year 2026 and it's not even close

title: SUPERHOT
body: SUPERHOT is a great 9/10 game. A very short experience with a unique gimmick and a mind bending story. You can finish this game in under two hours and refund it but don't you dare do that. Devs have truly earned your money since this game is something you have probably never played before. Another banger game made with passion. Thank you for that.
verdict: Indie classic all I can say

title: METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN
body:
Metal Gear Solid Venom: The Phantom Masterpiece. Such a complicated piece of work. And still I would call this a masterpiece. MGSV is the final work from Konami and Kojima and you can clearly see their relationship falling apart in this game. It’s so sad that this is the outcome. If things didn’t turn the way they did this would probably be one of the best games ever made.

Firstly, the best thing about this game, the gameplay. Holy it’s so well done and good. Easily the best from all Metal Gear games I’ve played. The ways you can proceed with missions are incredible. Mostly the game just gives you an objective and tools that you can use to execute it. The freedom of stealth is such an amazing feeling. And the amount of stuff you can use. Insane work.

Graphics are incredible looking and sometimes even better than most triple A games these days. I know Fox Engine has a sad history but man imagine if things didn’t turn out the way they did between Konami and Kojima. Looks so good for a 2015 game.

The story is the pivotal point where the game shows its flaws but it’s still a great time in my opinion. One of the reasons why I liked it is probably the knowledge of the Metal Gear universe. This game is not made to be an entry point to the franchise at all. I was even lost with some of the Peace Walker stuff.

Most of the “bad” stuff is more like “weird”. For example the pacing of the story and some of the cutscenes. It makes me truly wonder why things are the way they are. But still it’s an amazing game. A Phantom Masterpiece.
verdict: Duran Duran is in this I can prove it

title: Poker Night at the Inventory
body:
Poker Night at the Inventory is a silly little poker game that will make you realize how much you suck at poker. For 10 bucks it "can" be a fun time and it "can" grant you even more fun with the TF2 items.

(I just wanna go home I'm so much on negative and can't get the stupid items.)
verdict: Play for the TF2 items, stay for the gameplay

title: ELDEN RING NIGHTREIGN The Forsaken Hollows
body: The new map looks amazing but the gameplay loop on that feels untuned. But other than that everything in this dlc is good. Using Shadow of the Erdtree enemies is okay I guess don't mind it that much. New characters are also pretty awesome even though we played the final dlc boss with the base characters. Speaking of the final boss, probably the best thing about this dlc. So cinematic love it. And the ost on that too man gave me chills. Overall I can recommend this. I see the hate when they decided not to include Shadow of the Erdtree weapons but don't really care that much. Banger boss fights and more Dark Souls stuff is always fun to see.

title: METAL GEAR SOLID V: GROUND ZEROES
body: Just a demo I don't know pretty good gameplay I guess. Save 2 random children and that's it.
verdict: No idea how to rate this

title: METAL GEAR SOLID 2: Sons of Liberty - Master Collection Version
body:
Metal Gear Solid 2 basically fixes every problem I had with the first game. The gameplay is more enjoyable by a mile. There is a lot more stealth in this game. Every other room doesn't need to be a boss battle. I think Kojima understood that when he started working on this. This time boss battles are much better and very fun to beat. Not too challenging either.

MGS2 introduced some of the most standard MGS gameplay mechanics which are perfect already on their first introduction. Superb achievement for a game this old. The only negative thing about gameplay might have been the backtracking but it wasn't a big deal since the areas were great.

PS2 graphics make MGS2 feel more alive and enjoyable. Characters have more emotions (and funny moments of course). Advancement in technology is a great plus and I would like to see that in MGS1 someday in the form of a remake or something.

The story is confusing and weird but it's cinema. The introduction of Raiden felt a little weird at first but over time I understand him now and Kojima's vision. Raiden boosts Snake’s status as one of the greatest video game characters. Snake as a side character works great in this context. Story is a philosophical journey which makes me want to play MGS4 so badly.

Another absolute Hideo game. Gotta play more.

title: METAL GEAR SOLID - Master Collection Version
body: Glad I finally played this game to the end. For a PS1 game this is 10/10 masterpiece. For me today it's something like 8/10. This come from the janky gameplay mechanics which are clearly justified with time. But the story is probably one of the best written and told stories I have ever experienced in video game format. Can't wait to play MGS2 next on my journey to beat all mainline Metal Gear Solid games. Absolute Hideo Game!

title: Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty
body:
Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, a gateway out of the ordinary. At the start I was wondering was this directed by Hideo Kojima. Stuff gets crazy really fast and I love it. "A spy-thriller adventure" is a good description for this. Some of the scenes make me feel like I need a movie about this. Phantom Liberty gives you path from the main story with some of the best written characters probably ever. Almost every interaction with the main cast made me feel like "man I don't wanna make these choices".  Almost made me tear up. Such a great story. Hard to compare to the base game's story though.

In terms of gameplay this innovates and expands on the base game mechanics very well. Least favorite part was probably the skill tree expansion. The upgrades were great but the gameplay innovations in the quests were on a next level for me. Especially on the last few main missions.

Can't leave this review without talking about the world and atmosphere. Even though Dogtown looked small on the map, the progression and missions made it feel larger and alive. The more broken city atmosphere was well delivered and loved to take screenshots of the views I had.

Overall it's peak. As I said it's hard for me to compare it to the base game. Such a different tone there. Play this after the base game since starting this takes you on a wild ride at the start.
verdict: How can a DLC make you tear up even on your second playthrough?

title: Cyberpunk 2077
body:
Playing this game made me realize this game was made for me, like spot on. The atmosphere, themes, world everything tickles my synthwave loving heart. Booting the game for the first time and tweaking graphic settings while "V" by Marcin Przybyłowicz bangs on the background I knew this game was made for me.

Easily the best thing about this game is the city. Every view can be a wallpaper for my desktop. Every time I went somewhere to do even the smallest side mission, I was amazed by the world and how everything was put into place to make me think about how beautiful this game can be.  Also made me want to watch more cyberpunk themed movies and series.

Second best thing I loved was the stealth. The ways how to approach a stealth segment were just incredible.  Also if things went south I was never mad about it. Getting caught never made me restart from a checkpoint since the switch to loud is very well made and enjoyable. As a Payday 2 stealth veteran this pleased me a lot.

Everything else was also good don't get me wrong. Very interesting story when it gets rolling about 6-8 hours in. Character development and choices made me pause the game many times to think them more throughout. (And also made me question the devs why would they allow me to do some things.) Soundtrack an absolute banger. Definitely enjoyed the original soundtrack more than the original radio songs. (Modded my own Cyberpunk themed playlist half way through the game but still listened to the official radio stations a lot.)

Glad I experienced this. What a large game. This really shows in the length of the end credits lol.

Now off to Phantom Liberty.
verdict: I play this so I can play Phantom Liberty

title: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
body:
When I started this game I was ready for the “This is Dark Souls 2 buddy” statement but now after finishing the main story I am very surprised how good this game was. The more you play this game, the more you will enjoy it, trust me. The start of your playthrough will be the most difficult one out of all the Dark Souls games. The HP reduction most notably is the one that bothers new players the most but there also was the adaptability stat and no moving when drinking estus. All of these were annoying, yes, but over time they made the game more interesting. Somehow death being more punishing was fun.

Also this game has very interesting game design choices that we have never seen in a Dark Souls game. Most of them were great and I’d love to see them adapted in the future. For example enemies which look exactly like the player phantoms you see in the game were a pleasant surprise even though lock on was disabled. Closing doors was also funny.

In Dark Souls 1 and 3 the connections in story and world have been amazing and make replaying them even more fun. In Dark Souls 2 the story feels disconnected from the other ones but I don’t consider that a bad thing since I enjoyed it. You can decide how a player on his first playthrough understands the plot of a new Souls game but I had a great time. However nothing still beats the lore connections between Dark Souls 1 and 3. That there is peak. Dark Souls 2 is just a great time.

But now the question is do I recommend this game? Yes, but no. Do not play this as your first Dark Souls game. Never. The gameplay feels way different from the other ones even though it can be great at times especially in the end. Probably just play this after the first Dark Souls. If you enjoyed DS1 with its jankiness, there is no reason not to give Dark Souls 2 a shot. Just get ready for a learning curve.
verdict: Peak Souls 2: Scholar of the First Peak

title: Castle Crashers®
body: Castle Crashers is simply a lot of casual fun with your buddies. You can turn off your brain and enjoy beating funny looking characters and have a great time. The game is a short one (at least the story is) but there isn't really anything to complain about it. A solid 7/10. A good game without anything mind blowing.
verdict: I know you've heard songs from this game

title: DARK SOULS™: REMASTERED
body:
Dark Souls and souls-like games in general take a different mindset. A mindset that can be only learned by playing these games. My souls journey started with Elden Ring and then continued to Dark Souls 3. Now after playing the first Dark Souls I can comfortably say that playing those games first is the most optimal and the best way for anyone to start playing soulsborne games.

Dark Souls is a masterpiece for its time. Almost everything in this game can sometimes feel a bit janky. But they were there to build a foundation for these types of games. I'm very happy that I finally experienced this classic and definitely recommend this game for those who have learned the mindset already.

Praise the sun! (even though I killed Solaire lmao)
verdict: I will play this with a dance pad

title: FINAL FANTASY XVI
body:
Loved this games combat. Probably best thing about it. (Almost) every new ability was great to use and adapt to my build. Combat encounters weren't boring and boss fights were peak.
Story and lore was confusing many times but it managed to keep me at the edge of my seat to the very end.

Basically every side quest and few of the main quest were very boring to me. Most of them were just very basic where you didn't do anything new and interesting. Collect some stuff kill some basic enemies and return to the NPC. It was disappointing that some of the main quests where like this.

Performance was bad (probably half of that caused by my low PC specs) but it was playable. Some of the larger areas made fps drop under 30. The boss fights shined with sometimes over 60 fps.

Overall the game was great. Very Devil May Cry-like. A lot of "hype moments and aura" lol.

title: Bloodborne - Game of the Year Edition
body:
We all know Bloodborne is considered one of the best games there is. And all of that glaze is true. It has the greatest 3rd person combat. I’ve played this game like 3-4 times almost back-to-back, bought the soundtrack on vinyl and a cool hoodie. I love this world, its atmosphere, the themes, the passion FromSoftware put into this. It is so sad that PlayStation does almost nothing with this IP. The movie is one of my most anticipated things as of now. I just want more. Jacksepticeye wants more. People want more Bloodborne.

But what makes this game’s combat one of the greatest of all time? Well, every weapon is a fun and valid option. They are also super unique, every single one of them. The trick weapon system is one of the coolest mechanics in the gaming period. With Bloodborne's fast paced soulsborne combat the fighting just feels incredible. And on top of that add the bosses, especially from The Old Hunters DLC. Lady Maria is the second greatest boss fight in any game in my opinion (only next to the Nameless King ofc). Everything in the gameplay is just so fluid. I know people complain about Blood Vials but I didn’t see it as a big of an issue. Yeah it’s annoying to go and farm heals after losing to a peak boss but it also makes you more mentally prepared to fight them again.

Soulsborne games keep me so easily hooked. One of the most replayable franchises for sure. Bloodborne is easily in the top 2 best soulsborne games next to Elden Ring. These games are simply special. And super popular. I’m happy about that.

title: Devil May Cry
body:
Devil May Cry kinda like the first Metal Gear Solid. The birth of the franchise and pioneer of the genre. It’s an okay ride with all of its clunkiness. The overall gameplay is great but some of the segments really showcase its age. I really liked the levels and their layout and concepts (or should I say the world?). Dante is a great main character. No wonder they made six games with this fella. The story is… whatever I guess. It’s a base for the future. People don’t really play DMC for the story I think. (I might be wrong, not a fan here.)

Really looking forward to finishing the trilogy but I have heard “some” things about Devil May Cry 2. Really interested to see how the gameplay evolves throughout the games.
verdict: Motivated after the Netflix series Season 2 (it was really good btw)

title: Demon's Souls (PlayStation 5)
body:
The one that started it all, remade. As someone new to this game both this and the original version are pretty much equally good. If you would like to experience Demon’s Souls for the first time I would say go for the one that interests you more. I don’t really get all the hate this game gets. It’s pretty much the same game as the original, only made stunningly beautiful with the PlayStation 5 graphics. Some people say it loses its charm. If you think the same, go play the original. I just like them both equally.

Demon’s Souls is as addictive as any other soulsborne game for me. It makes you feel the same things like any other soulsborne game while you make your build or discover new areas. The worlds/levels system isn’t annoying at all, only the world tendency is the one that everyone thinks is weird.

The only negatives I have with this game are probably just that the bosses are pretty easy at times and the item burden system is just annoying. Overall a solid soulsborne game like any other. Demon’s Souls is the beginning and it shows. And I kinda like the uniqueness of it.
verdict: We all know we proudly glazing the soundteam

title: Demon's Souls
body: Just check out my review of the PlayStation 5 version. Pretty much the same game.

title: Marvel's Wolverine
body:
This game would probably be a 7/10 if the combat wasn’t this good. Marvel’s Wolverine feels like an Insomniac coded game as it should be but it feels like a bit lackluster compared to the peak that is the Marvel’s Spider-Man games. The game is very linear even though some areas may look like they have a lot of things going on. Those complaints about the “blue lines” online are completely invalid in my opinion. There is a completely valid reason for them to exist.

But yeah, this game is easily carried by the combat. Funny to say it but it really makes you feel like Wolverine. Especially on those wave based optional challenges shredding through the enemies aggressively is super fun. Skill trees are great with fun new additions to your kit. Those randomly happening team up kills straight from Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 are as satisfying as they were in that game as well. Fighting as Wolverine perfected.

That’s about it for the really good stuff. As I said, the game is linear. It doesn’t by itself make the game bad but everything combined with that makes it a bit of a disappointing experience. There aren’t a lot of things to do outside of following the story. Only a few collectibles and the challenges I mentioned previously. The story itself is okay, maybe pretty good even. It’s an interesting take on Logan but doesn’t really keep you that hooked. The characters are also just pretty good. Some better, some worse.

Overall Marvel’s Wolverine is a solid game. Combat carries the experience. Don’t pay the full price.
